text: Captions cut for every screen shape, from one file. Overtone stores each spoken word once, with its time and speaker, and cuts captions separately for each picture shape: 16:9 and 9:16 by default, or any aspect you name. A CLI makes the file from your subtitles, audio or video. A video.js plugin shows the cut that fits the player. Re-cut subtitles you already have. Offline, no API key, no ffmpeg (Node.js 22.12 or newer): curl -O https://download.blender.org/demo/movies/ToS/subtitles/TOS-en.srt npx overtone-captions recut TOS-en.srt You get TOS-en.overtone.json , .horizontal and .vertical .vtt and .srt files, and a transcript. Word times are estimated from the cues. Caption a video from its audio. This needs ffmpeg and provider API keys (OpenAI and Azure AI Speech by default; overtone providers lists the variables). --dry-run shows where the audio goes and the estimated cost, and sends nothing: npm install -g overtone-captions overtone transcribe talk.mp4 --language en --context " Panel about urban cycling " --dry-run overtone transcribe talk.mp4 --language en --context " Panel about urban cycling " --local runs offline instead, with whisper.cpp and Ollama. Show the captions in video.js: import videojs from 'video.js' ; import 'video.js/dist/video-js.css' ; import 'videojs-overtone' ; import 'videojs-overtone/themes/base.css' ; import 'videojs-overtone/themes/clean.css' ; videojs ( 'my-video' ) . overtone ( { src : 'talk.overtone.json' } ) ; Why Most captions are cut once, for one screen, by filling each line to a length limit. The 16:9 cut is too wide for a 9:16 phone video, lines end on "the" or "of", and two speakers share a caption. Overtone keeps a cut per screen shape in one file. The cuts follow reading rules: lines avoid ending on weak words, names and numbers stay together, each speaker gets their own caption, and pauses become line or caption breaks, so viewers who cannot hear a hesitation can read it. The same words and times from a NASA interview, cut for 9:16 (22 characters × 2 lines): the 2004 class. Jim, thank you for joining us. It's great to be here, Allard. Thanks. Jim, thank you for joining us. It's great to be here, Allard. Thanks. through you? Okay. A little about me: I grew up in Eugene, Oregon. I joined the Okay. A little about me: I grew up in Eugene, Oregon. I joined the Astronaut Corps Why a new format instead of WebVTT or TTML: those store finished cues, so a player can only rewrap them. .overtone.json stores each word once, plus any number of cuts that point to those words. Export WebVTT or SRT per cut when you need a standard file. Why not WhisperX, stable-ts or a hosted speech API: they give good words and times, often cheaper. Overtone adds the caption layout on top. overtone recut re-cuts their SRT or WebVTT output, so you can keep your engine. The LLM never sets timestamps: each word takes its time from the engines.
